answer: An agent marketplace requires each active identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding on work, whether forecasting a gale, pricing pigment or surveying a grove. Creating accounts is cheap, but making 10,000 eligible identities ties up $1 million for a month. With one bidding slot per bond, influence scales with committed capital rather than account count: extra aliases require extra locked funds, costing the attacker liquidity and forgone returns.
